newsitem.title: USA: Kitty Hawk expects IPO to be a success. [CORRECTED 07:25 GMT 5/10]
newsitem.headline: Kitty Hawk expects IPO to be a success. [CORRECTED 07:25 GMT 5/10]

text.p: After a false start last year, air cargo company Kitty Hawk Inc officials said this week they were confident that their initial public offering scheduled to be sold on October 8 would be a success.
"This is a very expensive business and you have to finance it one way or another," Tilmon Reeves, Kitty Hawk president, told the Cargo Facts Used Aircraft Symposium here this week.

Last year's attempted offering was scrapped as market conditions deterioated, Reeves said. Dallas-based Kitty Hawk is an all-cargo airline and just got a contract with the United States Postal Service to handle Christmas mail during 11 busy days in December, according to Cargo Facts newsletter.

But he added that "Kitty Hawk expanded to become much more viable than last year." The company was able to attract nationally known underwriters led by Smith, Barney Inc instead of the regional firms that had been managers.
The Smith Barney syndicate said that Kitty Hawk will be offering 3.0 million shares. The price range has been set at $12 to $14.
Proceeds will be used to buy seven Boeing Co 727-200s (Corrects type of aircraft from 747-200s), pay down debt, pay for some heavy maintenance and possibly make some acquisitions.
Kitty Hawk currently flies eight Boeing 727s, five Douglas DC-9 and nine Convair 600/640Fs.
